name: The Hartford

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (The Hartford Financial Services Group logo.svg)

description: The Hartford sells business insurance (small business, middle and large business, global specialty including Navigators and reinsurance) mainly through independent agents and brokers, personal auto and home insurance sold mostly to members of AARP under an exclusive licence running to 2032, and group benefits (disability, life, paid family leave) sold through employers. It earns premiums and invests the float, so profit is underwriting result plus investment income; workers' compensation, general liability and group disability are its long-tail bread and butter. Employee Benefits is a steady insurer-style margin business (core earnings margin 8.2 percent), not a property-casualty one. It agreed on 2026-06-03 to sell its Hartford Funds mutual fund and ETF asset manager (AUM $154 billion) to Wellington, a rare case of a P&C insurer exiting asset management.

businessLines.name: Business Insurance
businessLines.how: Commercial insurance sold mostly through retail and wholesale agents and brokers to businesses of every size (small business averages under $5 thousand per policy): workers compensation, general liability, property, package, commercial auto, professional liability, bonds, marine and assumed reinsurance; annual premiums ($13,883M earned premiums). Combined ratio 88.3 percent.

businessLines.name: Personal Insurance
businessLines.how: Sells auto, homeowners and personal umbrella cover to individuals, mostly through an exclusive licence with AARP (about 38 million members; agreement through 2032); AARP-program earned premiums were $3.4 billion in 2025. Annual renewing premiums sold direct and through agents. Combined ratio 91.9 percent (2024: 99.1; 2023: 107.5).

businessLines.name: Employee Benefits
businessLines.how: Employers pay premiums for group disability (short and long term), paid family leave, group life and supplemental health cover, renewed annually, and Hartford earns the margin between premiums and claims; 2025 core earnings margin 8.2 percent.

businessLines.name: Hartford Funds
businessLines.how: Earns asset-based management and distribution fees on mutual funds, ETFs and life-and-annuity separate accounts it manages for third parties (AUM $154,229M at 2025-12-31). Agreed 2026-06-03 to be sold to Wellington Management: $300M cash at closing plus contingent payments of 95 percent of after-tax available cash for about seven years (payments end once NPV at 11 percent plus upfront reaches $2.1 billion; if under $1.5 billion at year seven, continue up to eight more quarters); expected to close Q1 2027.

businessLines.name: Property & Casualty Other Operations
businessLines.how: Run-off of old asbestos, environmental and other claims; no new premium; a cost line, not a business.

businessLines.name: Corporate
businessLines.how: Not a business: debt and equity financing costs, purchase-accounting items, run-off structured settlements and M&A costs.

brands.name: AARP Program (exclusive licence to market Hartford personal auto, home and umbrella to AARP members)
brands.note: about $3.4 billion of 2025 earned premiums, roughly 83 percent of Personal Insurance revenue of $4,088M (ratio is earned premium vs segment revenue, approximate)

brands.name: Navigators Group (acquired 2019; in Business Insurance global specialty)
brands.note: premiums not broken out in the pages read

brands.name: Hartford Funds Management Group (being sold to Wellington)
brands.note: 3.9 percent of segment revenue, 5.5 percent of segment net income, 2025

measures.name: Cash-earnings yield
measures.long: Cash earnings (operating cash flow - capex - stock pay) / market value
measures.note: An insurer's operating cash flow includes premiums it holds (float) until claims are paid, so its cash yields run high and swing with how fast it is growing.

measures.name: FCF yield
measures.long: Free cash flow (operating cash flow - capex) / market value
measures.note: An insurer's operating cash flow includes premiums it holds (float) until claims are paid, so its cash yields run high and swing with how fast it is growing.
